description_full: Saputo Inc. produces, markets, and distributes dairy products in Canada, the United States, Australia, and the United Kingdom. The company offers mozzarella and cheddar; specialty cheeses, such as ricotta, provolone, parmesan, goat cheese, feta, havarti, snacking, romano, string, blue, and soft and processed cheeses; and brie, camembert, brick, colby, farmer, munster, monterey jack, and fresh curd. It also provides fluid milk, cream, yogurt, sour cream, cottage cheese, and ice cream mixes; and butter and butter blends, flavored cream, dips, half and half, whipping cream, value-added beverages, creamers, coffee beverages, aerosol whipped toppings, almond and oat milk, and aseptic food products and beverages. In addition, the company offers dairy ingredients, including milk powder, whey powder, lactose, and whey protein concentrates, as well as lactoferrin and infant formula; spreads and oils; demineralized whey, lactose, casein, galacto-oligosaccharides, dairy ingredient blends, and nutritional products; and distributes fine imported cheese to specialty stores, and dairy and non-dairy products manufactured by third parties, as well as dairy alternative products. It serves customers in the retail, foodservice, and industrial markets. The company sells its products under the Saputo, Armstrong, Alexis de Portneuf, Bari, Cogruet, DuVillage 1860, Kingsey, Shepherd Gourmet Dairy, Stella, Woolwich Goat Dairy, Dairyland, Neilson, Nutrilait, Baxter, Scotsburn, Trutaste, Milk2Go/Lait's Go, Baileys, Heluva Good, Black Creek, Frigo, Frigo Cheese Heads, Lugano, Montchevre, Mozzeria, Saputo Gold, Treasure Cave, DairyStar, Friendship Dairies, Caboolture, CHEER, Cracker Barrel, Devondale, Great Ocean Road, Liddells, Mersey Valley, Mil Lel, Murray Goulburn Ingredients, Sungold, Tasmanian Heritage, Cathedral City, Clover, Country Life, Davidstow, Frylight, Wensleydale Creamery, Vitalite, and Sheese brands. Saputo Inc. was founded in 1954 and is headquartered in Montreal, Canada.

financial_summary: Saputo Inc. is a large-cap consumer defensive business with a $12.6B market cap on $12.3B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at -2% over the past three years, and a shrinking top line is the hardest headwind any business can overcome.
Returns on capital run at 6% against a 7% cost of capital, which means the business is destroying value with every dollar it reinvests, with gross margins sitting at 31%.

The business throws off $819M in free cash flow — roughly 7 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 2.24× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, leverage is comfortably conservative at 1.7× net debt/EBITDA, and interest coverage runs at 9.3×.

Management returns a meaningful 5.6% of market cap to owners through dividends and buybacks, a strong signal of disciplined capital allocation, and insiders hold 42% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is.

news_headlines.title: Saputo Inc. (OTCMKTS:SAPIF) Stock Now Rated “Moderate Buy” by Wall Street Brokerages

sect: Its 6% operating margin is roughly in line with the Consumer Defensive median (7%).
It earns less of the sector's profit than its revenue share would suggest (0.74x).
It accounts for 0.4% of sector revenue and 0.3% of sector operating profit.
The sector is fragmented and competitive (HHI 0.07 across 172 companies in the universe; the top four hold 38% of revenue), so pricing power is hard to come by.
mkt: The shares are roughly flat over the past year excluding the latest month.
The price sits near the top of its 52-week range, 1% below the high.
With annualised volatility of 26% and a beta of 0.45, it is more defensive than the market, though its beta has shifted (1y -0.51 vs 5y 0.33), so read it loosely.
Trading is thin (about $928K a day), below the $1.0M liquidity floor flagged; building a position would move the price.
In past sell-offs it fell 33% in the 2020 crash and 22% in the 2022 bear market.
val: The stock trades 26% below its DCF fair value of $43.22, a meaningful margin of safety.
The fair-value models corroborate one another (dispersion 8%), and the Monte Carlo range runs $32.80 to $58.57 (P10-P90).
On multiples it looks expensive against Consumer Defensive peers: P/E 24.8 vs 18.3 (sector median).
Earnings yields are mixed: an FCF yield of 6.5% (above the risk-free rate) and an EBIT/EV of 4.9% (vs the 8% bar).
The price implies 3.5% annual cash-flow growth, 4pp less than the model expects.
prof: ROIC of 6% falls short of the cost of capital of 6.6%, so growth at these returns destroys value; returns have been steady (CV 0.28).
It runs a 31% gross margin and converts 7% of revenue into free cash flow.
Earnings quality looks solid: a Piotroski score of 8/9 and cash conversion of 2.24x.
ROE of 10% comes mostly from margins and asset turnover rather than leverage (2.0x equity multiplier).
hlth: Leverage is moderate at 1.7x net debt to EBITDA ($311.2M of cash against $2.3B of debt), above the 1.5x gate, with interest covered 9.3x.
No distress or manipulation flags (Altman Z 3.7, in the safe zone).
growth: Revenue has compounded at -2.0% over 3 years.
At current returns, reinvesting 39% of profits supports about 2.4% a year of fundamental growth, too little to drive meaningful growth.
own: Insiders own 41.9%, meaningful skin in the game, and institutions hold 34%.
It returns 5.6% a year to shareholders (3.8% in buybacks and 1.8% in dividends).
It has paid a dividend for 12 consecutive years.
people: With about 19,200 employees, each generates about $641K of revenue, 1.3x the Consumer Defensive median.
That works out to $43K of free cash flow per employee.
CEO pay is $3.4M (5x revenue per employee).
